name: Italy
title: The first title goes to Farina
story: Alfa Romeo dominates the inaugural World Championship. Giuseppe Farina wins at Monza and becomes the first champion, ahead of team-mate Juan Manuel Fangio.

name: Spain
title: Fangio begins his dynasty
story: Fangio wins at Pedralbes and takes his first title. Ferrari has broken Alfa Romeo’s winning streak during the season; the championship is already becoming an engineering contest as well as a driving one.

name: Germany
title: Ascari’s year
story: With the championship run to Formula Two rules, Alberto Ascari and Ferrari dominate. Victory at the Nürburgring secures his first championship.

name: Switzerland
title: Ascari repeats
story: Ascari wins at Bremgarten and retains the championship. This is the last season of the championship’s Formula Two regulations before the 2.5-litre formula arrives.

name: Switzerland
title: One champion, two teams
story: Fangio wins the title after racing for Maserati and then Mercedes during the same season. The streamlined and open-wheel versions of the Mercedes W196 show how much bodywork could depend on the circuit.

name: Great Britain
title: Moss wins at home
story: Stirling Moss takes his first championship Grand Prix victory at Aintree, leading a Mercedes sweep. His rivalry with Fangio is also a relationship between team-mates and a pupil and mentor.

name: Italy
title: Collins hands Fangio a lifeline
story: Peter Collins gives his Ferrari to Fangio after Fangio’s own car develops trouble. Shared drives are permitted in this era; Fangio’s shared second place secures the title.

name: Germany
title: Fangio’s Nürburgring masterpiece
story: A slow pit stop leaves Fangio chasing the Ferraris. He reels them in to win in the Maserati 250F, sealing his fifth title in his final championship Grand Prix victory.

name: Morocco
title: Hawthorn wins the title; Moss wins the race
story: Mike Hawthorn’s second place is enough to beat Moss to the championship by one point. Vanwall takes the first constructors’ championship. Stuart Lewis-Evans suffers burns here and dies afterwards; the title story has a tragic backdrop.

name: United States
title: Brabham pushes to the finish
story: Jack Brabham runs out of fuel and pushes his Cooper across the line, finishing fourth and becoming champion. Bruce McLaren takes his first victory as rear-engined cars overturn the established order.

name: Portugal
title: Cooper confirms the revolution
story: Brabham wins at Porto, his fifth consecutive victory of the season. Cooper’s small rear-engined cars have made the front-engined layout obsolete at the sharp end of the grid.

name: Italy
title: Von Trips and spectators are killed at Monza
story: Championship leader Wolfgang von Trips collides with Jim Clark on the second lap of Monza’s high-speed combined road-and-banked circuit. Von Trips and spectators die. Phil Hill wins the race and championship in a sombre aftermath; F1 abandons the banking after this tragedy.

name: South Africa
title: Hill survives; Clark’s Lotus does not
story: Jim Clark needs victory to take the title, but an oil leak ends his race. Graham Hill wins for BRM and becomes champion in the final round.

name: Italy
title: Clark and Chapman change the template
story: Clark wins at Monza and clinches the championship in the Lotus 25. Its monocoque construction points toward the structure that will become standard in Formula 1.

name: Mexico
title: Surtees wins an extraordinary three-way finale
story: Clark’s late engine trouble changes the title picture, and John Surtees finishes second to become champion. Surtees remains the only person to win world championships on both two and four wheels.

name: Germany
title: Clark’s second championship
story: Clark wins at the Nürburgring and seals his second title. In the same year he also wins the Indianapolis 500: a remarkable bridge between two very different forms of racing.

name: Italy
title: Brabham wins in his own name
story: Ludovico Scarfiotti wins for Ferrari, while Jack Brabham clinches the title despite retiring. The new three-litre engine formula helps Brabham become the only driver to win the championship in a car bearing his own name.

name: Italy
title: Clark’s comeback; Surtees’ last win
story: After losing a lap with a puncture, Clark fights back into contention before running short of fuel. Surtees wins for Honda after a close finish with Brabham. The race rewards watching beyond the winner.

name: Mexico
title: Graham Hill steadies Lotus
story: Hill wins the finale and the title in a season in which Lotus loses Jim Clark in a Formula Two accident. Wings and commercial sponsorship are changing the appearance and business of the sport.

name: Italy
title: A slipstreaming finish
story: Jackie Stewart wins at Monza and clinches his first championship. The leading four cars finish almost together: an illustration of the tow before later chicanes reshape the circuit.

name: United States
title: Rindt’s posthumous championship
story: Emerson Fittipaldi wins his first Grand Prix. Jacky Ickx can no longer overhaul Jochen Rindt, who was killed at Monza; Rindt becomes Formula 1’s only posthumous world champion.

name: Italy
title: Five cars, almost one finish
story: Peter Gethin wins a five-way sprint to the line. Stewart has already secured the championship, but this is the season’s extraordinary race to watch: Monza’s slipstreaming era at its most compressed.

name: Italy
title: Fittipaldi becomes champion
story: Fittipaldi wins at Monza and secures the title for Lotus. At 25, he sets a youngest-champion record that will stand until Fernando Alonso’s breakthrough in 2005.

name: Italy
title: Stewart’s third and final title
story: Ronnie Peterson wins; Stewart recovers from a puncture to finish fourth and clinch the championship. Stewart’s importance extends beyond results to his campaign for safer circuits and medical facilities.

name: Netherlands
title: Purley tries to save Williamson
story: Roger Williamson’s car overturns and catches fire on lap eight at Zandvoort. David Purley stops and repeatedly tries to turn the wreck over and fight the flames, but marshals are unable to reach Williamson in time. Jackie Stewart wins a race remembered for Williamson’s death and Purley’s rescue attempt.

name: United States
title: Fittipaldi versus Regazzoni
story: Carlos Reutemann wins at Watkins Glen. Fittipaldi finishes fourth and takes the title as rival Clay Regazzoni struggles; McLaren wins its first drivers’ championship.

name: Italy
title: Lauda brings Ferrari back
story: Clay Regazzoni wins and Lauda finishes third, enough to secure Ferrari’s first drivers’ title since 1964. Lauda’s analytical approach becomes central to Ferrari’s revival.

name: Japan
title: Hunt, Lauda and a rain-soaked reckoning
story: Lauda withdraws in dangerous conditions, weeks after surviving his Nürburgring fire. Hunt finishes third and takes the title by a single point. The result cannot be separated from the drivers’ choices about risk.

name: United States
title: Lauda’s second title
story: James Hunt wins at Watkins Glen, while Lauda’s fourth place secures the championship. Lauda is about to leave Ferrari; winning a title does not mean a partnership is harmonious.

name: Italy
title: Ground effect, and a devastating cost
story: Mario Andretti clinches the title in the season of the Lotus 79’s ground-effect dominance. Ronnie Peterson is injured in the start-line accident and dies the next day. Niki Lauda is the official race winner after penalties.

name: Italy
title: Ferrari’s one-two settles the championship
story: Jody Scheckter wins ahead of team-mate Gilles Villeneuve and secures the title. Ferrari will wait until Schumacher in 2000 for its next drivers’ championship.

name: Canada
title: Jones prevails in a bitter rivalry
story: Alan Jones wins and becomes champion for Williams. His collision with Nelson Piquet at the first start, followed by a restarted race, adds heat to an already combative title fight.

name: Caesars Palace
title: Piquet takes the title in a car park
story: Jones wins the finale in Las Vegas. Piquet’s fifth place is enough to beat Carlos Reutemann by one point, at a temporary circuit laid out beside the Caesars Palace hotel.
